persistence_source.rule: y_hat(t+k) = A(t) for every k; trajectory score = A(t)
persistence_source.input: observed attack_present at window t, read from data/processed/states_v2/<day>_states_v2.csv at (metadata timestamp - 10s)
incompatible_artifacts_excluded: archive/train_persistence_baseline.py and models/world_model/persistence_baseline/* — state REGRESSION persistence (MAE/RMSE/R2, 19 features, old temporal_benchmark); not an attack-label forecaster and not on this benchmark

split_policy: chronological held-out day; train days Feb-14/Feb-15/Feb-28 each split chronologically 85% train / 15% validation (VAL_RATIO=0.15); Mar-2 entirely held out

threshold_policy.persistence: none — deterministic rule, no tunable threshold
threshold_policy.logistic_regression: validation-only F1 argmax over np.arange(0.01, 0.99, 0.01), frozen in Task 2
threshold_policy.v4_world_model: validation-only F1 argmax over the same grid, frozen in Task 1
threshold_policy.rationale: each model keeps its own legitimate validation-derived threshold; data, targets, test set and metric definitions are identical

horizons.point_forecast_exclusion_reason: the frozen V4 reference has no K=4 result; LR K=4 is reported separately as point_forecast_secondary_lr_only

metric_definitions.precision/recall/f1: sklearn binary, zero_division=0, at the model's frozen threshold
metric_definitions.roc_auc: sklearn roc_auc_score on the raw score (threshold independent); for persistence the score is binary, so the curve is degenerate
metric_definitions.trajectory_score_v4: max over rollout probabilities probs[:, 1:K+1] of one model
metric_definitions.trajectory_score_lr: max over K independently trained horizon-specific models

v4_provenance_caveat: The V4 checkpoint was trained on data/processed/temporal_benchmark_v2/multistep_K5 (single-day Feb-28, scaler n=2384) while the frozen reference evaluation feeds it multiday_benchmark_K5 arrays scaled by a different StandardScaler (n=8575). This comparison uses the frozen V4 reference exactly as defined; the caveat is preserved, not repaired. See docs/V4_REFERENCE_BASELINE.md section 12.
